identity_access_agents_auth_scope_descri:
Agent Identities are API keys with policy-based permissions. Each identity defines which MCP servers, Skills, LLMs, and Obot API capabilities an agent can access.

When you create an identity, Obot issues an API key tied to those permissions. Every request made with that key is evaluated against the identity's policy, giving you centralized access control and consistent permission enforcement across agent workloads.

identity_access_scim_app_help: In {provider}, create a SCIM 2.0 application, and enter the base URL shown above and the bearer token. This step is done once {provider} sends Obot a request.
identity_access_scim_assign_help: Assign everyone who should be able to sign in to the SCIM application in {provider}, which then provisions them in Obot.
identity_access_scim_bearer_expired: The bearer token expired on {date}, so {provider}'s SCIM requests fail. Rotate the token, update it in {provider}, and retry the failed provisioning tasks there.
identity_access_scim_bearer_expiring: The bearer token expires on {date}. Rotate it before then, and update it in {provider}: the current token keeps working for up to a day after the rotation.
identity_access_scim_connected_body: {provider} provisions users and groups through SCIM. Users it has not provisioned can still sign in until SCIM is enforced.
identity_access_scim_copy_token_now: Copy the token now. It is shown only once. Enter the base URL and the token in the SCIM application in {provider}.
identity_access_scim_delete_groups_note: They grant nothing, so no one loses access. The groups will still exist in {provider} but will no longer be known to Obot.
identity_access_scim_enable_note: This cannot be undone. Obot stops fetching groups from {provider} at sign-in, so until {provider} pushes a referenced group, it keeps its current members, including anyone removed from it in {provider}. The bearer token for {provider} is shown next, only once.
identity_access_scim_enforce_disables: Enforcing SCIM disables these users. Provisioning them later re-enables them with their account and data.
identity_access_scim_enforce_disables_us: Enforcing disables the {users} that it has not provisioned. Group memberships do not change, and nothing is deleted from the users.
identity_access_scim_enforce_help: Once SCIM is enforced, only accounts that {provider} provisioned can sign in.
identity_access_scim_enforce_note_none: This cannot be undone. Only provisioned users can sign in with {provider} afterwards.
identity_access_scim_enforce_note_some: This cannot be undone. Enforcing disables {users} that {provider} has not provisioned, and only provisioned users can sign in with {provider} afterwards.
identity_access_scim_enforced_body: Signing in with {provider} requires an account that {provider} provisioned.
identity_access_scim_every_group_pushed: Every referenced group has been pushed.
identity_access_scim_groups_migrated: Push each referenced group from {provider} under exactly the name shown, renaming it there first if needed, or remove its references.
identity_access_scim_groups_new: Push the groups from {provider} that roles and policies should be granted to. More can be pushed at any time.
identity_access_scim_issue_token_note: The token is shown only once. Copy it into the SCIM application of the identity provider. It expires after a year, so rotate it before then.
identity_access_scim_move_body: Obot fetches each user's groups from {provider} when they sign in. Enabling SCIM lets {provider} provision users, account status, groups, and memberships instead, and Obot stops fetching groups at sign-in. It cannot be undone.
identity_access_scim_move_still_signin: Everyone can still sign in once SCIM is enabled. Enforcing SCIM, a later step, will allow only accounts provisioned by {provider} to sign in.

identity_access_scim_no_users_yet: {provider} has not provisioned any users yet.

identity_access_scim_not_setup_move: An auth provider that supports SCIM and already fetches groups from its directory at sign-in can be moved to SCIM here.

identity_access_scim_reload: Reload this page to review the move to SCIM.
identity_access_scim_revoke_current_note: Use this when the token has leaked. A new token is issued, and both the current and the previous token stop working at once, so provisioning fails until the identity provider uses the new one.

identity_access_scim_rotate_token_msg: Issue a new SCIM bearer token?
identity_access_scim_rotate_token_note: The current token keeps working for a day, or until it expires or you revoke it, so you can update the identity provider without failed requests.
identity_access_scim_setup_banner: {provider} provisions users and groups through SCIM, and SCIM is not enforced yet. Continue setup on Identity & Access → Auth Providers → SCIM: create the SCIM app in {provider} with the base URL and token, assign users, push groups, and enforce SCIM.
